post.description:
Create a new user using external SSO.

---

User email has to be unique across the Aurora app.

Please note that in contrast to the [Invite User](ref:inviteuser) endpoint this will not send the user an email to join the user. The created user account will hence not be able to set their password.

Creating a user without inviting them is a required step if you are using SSO through OpenID connect to authenticate the users before accessing Aurora's application. This will allow your users to use Aurora without having to type in their username and password before doing so, but require you to run an OpenID Connect server (proving the Identity Provider functionality to Aurora). See [OpenID Connect specification](http://openid.net/developers/specs/) for more detail.

Please note that certain identity providers such as SalesForce, represent their user and organization IDs differently in the UI compared to what is sent in actual API requests. If you are using SalesForce as the identity provider with the OpenID Connect standard, please specify the long 18 character user and organization IDs when creating a user. See [here](http://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/1653/what-are-salesforce-ids-composed-of) for instructions on how to convert a 15 character ID to an 18 character one.

parameters.description: The ID of the tenant to create the user for.

email.description: Email address of the user. Must be unique within the Aurora system.

external_provider_id.description: The full identifying URL identifying this user on the identity provider's system. Ex. "https://test.salesforce.com/id/00556000000X3J3AFA/00540000001ulvMAEA"

role_id.description: Unique ID identifying the user's role. Choose between IDs for the following global roles [`"Limited Team Member"`, `"Team Member"`, `"Admin"`] and any custom roles defined for the tenant. Defaults to the ID for `"Team Member"`. To view all available roles, see [List Roles](ref:listroles).

Returns a list of roles.

---

Roles are returned sorted in ascending order with custom roles listed first if any exist, then ordered alphabetically by name.

For more on custom roles, see our [Help Center](https://help.aurorasolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/11459813328787).

parameters.description: The ID of the tenant to get roles for.

custom.description: Whether or not the role is custom for the tenant. Global roles are derived from previously existing user levels and present for all tenants.

post.description:
Uploads or replaces the logo image for a partner.

The request body should contain the raw binary image data (not JSON).
A Content-Disposition header is required to specify the filename.

Accepted formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, HEIC, WEBP.
The image will be converted to WebP format.

If the partner already has a logo, the previous logo will be replaced.

parameters.name: Content-Disposition
parameters.description: Must follow the format: attachment; filename="<filename>.<extension>"

get.description:
Retrieve a list of orders for a tenant.

Orders are returned sorted by time, with the newest orders first.
Without the page and per_page parameters, the first 100 orders will be returned.
If per_page is specified, a maximum of 250 orders will be returned.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The ID of the tenant to get orders for.

parameters.name: page

post.description:
Create a new project.

---

A project within Aurora contains important customer information such as the address, latitude/longitude. Aurora allows you to specify your primary key of a customer/client within Aurora's system under the field `external_provider_id`. This allows you to map your client/customer record to Aurora's project.

The address and latitude/longitude coordinates on the Project are designed to be as consistent as possible. They represent the location of the project but not necessarily the specific building that should have the solar installation.

You must pass in an address or latitude/longitude coordinates. Here are the different combinations for passing in an address and latitude/longitude coordinates:

- If you only pass the address, we will calculate the latitude/longitude coordinates from that address.
This latitude/longitude may or may not represent the actual building that should have the solar installation.

- If you only pass latitude/longitude coordinates that fall within the property line, we will calculate the address from these coordinates. We set the customer address to this calculated address.

- If you pass both the address and the latitude/longitude coordinates of the building that should have the solar installation, we will set them as passed in.

put.description:
Update the existing consumption profile for a project.

---

Each request must contain `utility_rate_escalation`, one of the energy consumption values below, or both.

---

**Energy consumption.** A request accepts *only one* of the following values.

- `monthly_energy`: An array of exactly 12 monthly energy values in kWh. Null values are allowed and represented as "null".

- `monthly_bill`: An array of exactly 12 monthly bill values, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`). Null values are allowed and represented as "null".

- `interval_data`: An array of exactly (8760, 8784, 17520, 17568, 35040, or 35136) energy values in kWh. Null values are allowed and represented as "null".
  - The array must contain at least 1 complete month of contiguous non-null values.
  - The first array value must correspond to the first interval of the year beginning at 1 January 00:00.

- `annual_energy`: The total annual energy consumption in kWh. Aurora distributes it across the year using a typical load profile for the project's location, so monthly values follow the expected seasonal variation.

- `annual_bill`: The total annual pre-solar electricity bill, denominated in the tenant's configured currency. Aurora finds the annual energy consumption whose bills, under the project's pre-solar utility rate, sum to this amount, then distributes that energy across the year in the same way as `annual_energy`.
  - The project must have a pre-solar utility rate. The conversion uses the rate set at the time of the request; changing the rate later does not change the consumption profile.

Bill inputs (`monthly_bill`, `annual_bill`) are converted to energy using energy and fixed charges only. Demand charges are not included in the conversion, so on a rate with demand charges the returned `monthly_bill` values are higher than the bills provided.

Annual inputs require a typical load profile for the project's location. The response returns `input_values` as null for every month, since all monthly values are estimated.

---

**Utility rate escalation.** `utility_rate_escalation` is independent of the energy consumption values. It can be sent on its own, which leaves the consumption profile unchanged, or together with one energy consumption value. If the request is rejected, neither is applied.

- `utility_rate_escalation`: The annual escalation of utility rates, as a percentage (`4.0` means 4%). New projects start with the tenant's default for the project's type and location. A value must fall within the tenant's configured minimum and maximum for the project, otherwise the request is rejected with a 422 error. The range is only checked when the value changes, so sending the project's current value is always accepted. `null` is treated as not provided, so the value cannot be reset to the tenant default through the API. Financing options that use an integration-provided escalation rate ignore this value.

Consumption profiles are only supported for residential projects.

post.description:
Uploads a utility bill document for a project and starts an asynchronous OCR parse of its contents. The file upload itself is handled synchronously inside this endpoint, so a `utility_bill_id` is returned immediately along with the `job_id` for the parse step.

The bill bytes are sent as a raw request body (not multipart/JSON), with the original filename carried in the `Content-Disposition` header. Accepted formats: PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP.

---

**Last-parse-wins semantics.** Each completed parse replaces the consumption data derived from any previously parsed bill on the same project — only the most recently parsed bill feeds the project's load profile. Because parse jobs run asynchronously and are not strictly FIFO, an earlier upload that finishes parsing after a later upload will become the active bill. Older bill files persist in storage but no longer contribute to the project's consumption values. This matches the behavior of the in-app utility bill upload UI.

Note that this is an asynchronous endpoint. See the [Asynchronous Endpoints](ref:asynchronous-endpoints) appendix for more info.

**Last-parse-wins semantics.** Only the most recently parsed bill feeds the project's load profile and consumption data. get.description:
Retrieve the summary of a design.

---

This action allows you to pass back Aurora design information into your own systems. You will likely call this endpoint after a user has modified a design within the Aurora application and intends to return back to the portal or primary application he/she originally came from (Salesforce, SugarCRM...).

The design summary contains a field called 'arrays'. The contents of the field is a JSON string containing details of the solar system designed. Each array is a group of solar modules that have the same roof face, module model, azimuth, pitch, orientation (portrait vs. landscape), MLPE (module level power electronics, such as microinverter or dc-optimizer) and which connect to the same MPPT within a string inverter. Example: let's assume you have a house with a simple gable roof ('A'-roof), where one side is south-facing and the other north. Furthermore, let's assume that that you install a 8kW system consisting of 32 x 250 Watt modules. 8 of them on the north-facing roof and 24 of them on the south-facing roof connecting to two different inverters. There would be 2 arrays in the design summary, one with "face = 1" and the other with "face = 2". Please note that the "face" IDs are not guaranteed to reflect the same directionality (i.E. face 1 is not guaranteed to be South), instead they are a way of grouping arrays located on the same roof face. The "face" IDs are not included in the layout DXF files.

Continuing the example above, connecting 8 of the 24 modules on the south-facing roof to microinverters, 8 to DC optimizers and stringing the remaining 8 to a central inverter would result in a total of 4 arrays in the design summary (one due to the roof face and 3 due to the usage of MLPE's and/or a central string inverter).

put.description:
Update the editable per-design system-loss settings.

---

The request body is a flat map of loss name to percentage. Only the losses you supply are
updated; all others are left unchanged (partial update). Values are percentages between 0
and 100, accepted to one decimal place.

Updating system losses **invalidates** the design's performance simulation. This endpoint
does **not** re-run the simulation — run it separately to recompute production. Until then,
`energy_production.up_to_date` on the [Design Summary](ref:retrievedesignsummary) will be
`false`.

### Locks

Some losses cannot be edited and a request to change them is rejected with `422`:

- **Financing lock** — when a financing product is selected for the design, that product
  dictates every loss. The whole update is rejected. This is reflected on read as
  `editable: false` / `locked_by_financier: "<code>"`, with every field `locked: true` and
  `disabled_reason: "financier"`.
- **Shading-engine lock** — when the shading engine is enabled, the `shading` loss is
  computed automatically and cannot be set manually. A request including `shading` is
  rejected, and on read that field is `locked: true` with
  `disabled_reason: "shading_engine_enabled"`.

### Mapping to loss_summary stages

Each editable setting affects exactly one `loss_summary` output stage on the Design Summary:

| Setting | `loss_summary` stage (`name`) |
| --- | --- |
| `soiling` | `irradiance_after_soiling_loss` |
| `snow` | `irradiance_after_snow_loss` |
| `shading` | `irradiance_after_shade_loss` |
| `mismatch` | `energy_after_mismatch_loss` |
| `connections` | `energy_after_connections_loss` |
| `wiring` | `energy_after_dc_wiring_loss` |
| `light_induced_degradation` | `energy_after_lid_loss` |
| `availability` | `energy_after_availability_loss` |
| `age` | `energy_after_age_loss` |
| `rating` | `energy_after_nameplate_loss` |
| `other` | `energy_after_other_loss` |

The remaining `loss_summary` stages are engine-computed and have no editable input.

get.description:
Retrieve summary of all roofs for a design.

---
In Aurora, a roof is a set of roof faces within 1 square foot of each other. A roof's area is the sum of its roof face areas. Note that the pitch for a roof is only returned if all faces in the roof have the same pitch.

Please note for simple roof faces in Aurora, roof edge types are not set automatically, and will need to be set manually when designing a roof. Roofs created with SmartRoof and AI Roof will automatically have edge types set.

We determine the shape of each roof face using the following heuristics in the order listed:
  - Flat: roof with 2:12 slope (9.46 degrees) or less
  - Monopitch: roof with a single face with a pitch greater than 2:12 (9.46 degrees)
  - Hip: roof where the length of hip edges is greater than the length of rake edges
  - Gable: roof with at least one rake

Units for all lengths and areas will be imperial or metric depending on the tenant setting in the Aurora app.

post.description:
Generate a CAD screenshot of a design on demand, without a user having to open the design and click the manual screenshot button.

---

Note that this is an asynchronous endpoint. See the [Asynchronous Endpoints](ref:asynchronous-endpoints) appendix for more info.

The design must have a completed [Irradiance Analysis](ref:irradiance-analysis) (panels mode) before a screenshot can be generated; the endpoint returns a 422 otherwise.

Once the job succeeds, the resulting image is delivered as a "CAD API Screenshot" asset, retrievable via the [List Design Assets](ref:listdesignassets) / [Retrieve Design Asset](ref:retrievedesignasset) endpoints, and an `asset_created` webhook fires for it — there is no separate download endpoint. Unlike the "CAD Auto Screenshot" produced when a design is saved, a CAD API Screenshot never replaces a prior screenshot of any kind; up to 10 can accumulate per design, after which the endpoint returns a 422.

Set a layer to `true` to show it or `false` to hide it; a layer not mentioned at all falls back to this API's own standard default (noted per property below) rather than the design's saved layer state -- this keeps results stable for fully automated callers who screenshot a design before anyone has reviewed or edited it.

post.description:
Reject a roof model that is awaiting review, so that it is not accepted and no credits are consumed.

> 🚧 **This permanently deletes the design and everything attached to it**: proposals, agreements, plan sets, financings, pricing, adders and design assets. It cannot be undone.
>
> AI Roof writes the model directly into the design, and the generated geometry cannot be removed on its own, so rejecting deletes the design. Use this only on a design created to receive an AI Roof model, not one you intend to keep.

---

Applies only to a model generated with `defer_auto_accept` set on [Run AI Roof](ref:runairoof), while it is still within its one hour review window. Once a model has been accepted, it can no longer be rejected.

Rejection and deletion are all-or-nothing. If the design cannot be deleted, this operation returns `409` and the model is **not** rejected: it stays awaiting review and will be accepted, and billed, when the review window elapses. Common causes are a completed permit request, a shared milestone, an applied financing, or a signed agreement. Clear the blocker and call again before the window elapses.

get.description:
Report whether the elevation (LIDAR/DSM) data selected for a design is out of date
relative to the imagery selected for that design, along with the capture date of
each and the imagery resolution.

---

Use this before running AI Roof to predict output quality: a design whose elevation
data is out of date relative to its imagery is likely to produce a poorer roof model.

Note that "out of date" is a comparison *between the two sources*, not a judgement
about whether either is current in absolute terms. Two sources captured at the same
time agree with each other even if both are old, so read `capture_date` alongside it.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The ID of the tenant that the design is part of.

parameters.name: design_id
parameters.description: The ID of the design to report LIDAR status for.

200.description: The current LIDAR status for the design.

reason.description:
Why no verdict is available. Null unless `status` is `unavailable`.
`lidar_data_unavailable`: the imagery or LIDAR for this design could not be
identified or is not yet usable, so there is nothing to compare.
`computation_failed`: the comparison could not be completed; retrying may succeed.

capture_date.description: Calendar date the imagery was captured, when reported by the provider.

resolution.description: Imagery resolution in centimetres per pixel, when reported by the provider.

capture_date.description:
Calendar date the elevation capture began, when available. For Aurora LIDAR
flights spanning multiple days this is the start of the window; the end date
is not returned. Resolution is not exposed for elevation data because the
stored point spacing may have been downsampled.

put.description: Update pricing for an existing design.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The ID of the tenant that the design is part of.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the design to update pricing details for.

pricing.description: Pricing fields to update. At least one field must be provided. `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, and `line_items` are mutually exclusive — provide one solar pricing field, not more than one. `line_items` sets per-component solar prices and sets the solar pricing mode to `price breakdown`. `storage_flat_system_price` and `storage_line_items` are mutually exclusive. Either storage field can be provided alone or alongside a solar pricing field. `heat_pump_flat_system_price` and `heat_pump_line_items` are mutually exclusive. Either heat pump field can be provided alone or alongside a solar or storage pricing field.

flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the design and sets the pricing mode to `flat system price`. Cannot be used with `price_per_watt` or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

price_per_watt.description: Sets the price per watt for the design and sets the pricing mode to `price per watt`. Cannot be used with `flat_system_price` or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`) per watt.

line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the design's solar price breakdown and sets the solar pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing solar line item in the design. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Cannot be used with `flat_system_price` or `price_per_watt`.

price.description: Price for one unit of the component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

storage_flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the storage design and sets the storage pricing mode to `flat system price`. Requires the design to have a storage design. Subject to the tenant's configured minimum/maximum storage flat price limits when set — a value outside those limits is rejected with a 422. Cannot be used with `storage_line_items`. Can be used alongside `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

storage_line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the storage price breakdown and sets the storage pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing storage line item. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Requires the design to have a storage design. Cannot be used with `storage_flat_system_price`. Can be used alongside `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, or `line_items`.

price.description: Price for one unit of the storage component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

heat_pump_flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the heat pump and sets the heat pump pricing mode to `flat system price`. Requires the design to have a heat pump. Subject to the tenant's configured minimum/maximum heat pump flat price limits when set — a value outside those limits is rejected with a 422. Cannot be used with `heat_pump_line_items`. Can be used alongside a solar or storage pricing field. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

heat_pump_line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the heat pump price breakdown and sets the heat pump pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing heat pump line item. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Requires the design to have a heat pump. Cannot be used with `heat_pump_flat_system_price`. Can be used alongside a solar or storage pricing field.

price.description: Price for one unit of the heat pump component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

up_to_date.description: Whether the attributes calculated by financial simulation are up-to-date

system_price.description: Total price the customer pays; includes the principal, downpayment and incentive grants. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

total_system_cost_before_financing_adjus.description: System cost from design pricing only, before financing-layer adjustments. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

cashflow_discount_rate.description: The interest rate (in %) used to compare future cashflows to present cashflows. Comes from the design's financing settings. Rounded to 4 decimal places.

Rounded to 4 decimal places.

inverter_life.description: The expected number of years until the inverter needs to be replaced. Comes from the design's financing settings.

year1_avoided_cost.description: The post-solar bill savings in the first year.

items.description: Each month's savings in the first year in dollars. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

lifetime_savings.description: Total savings over the entire life of your solar project in today's dollars. Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 2 decimal places. Takes into account the price of the system, the discount rate, any down payments, loan payments, PPA payments, lease payments, utility bill savings, incentives, interest, operations and maintenance, and all financial costs and benefits of going solar.

annual_cashflows.description: Yearly cashflows (in $) in and out as the customer owns their solar system. Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

incentive_values.description: The value of all incentives applicable to the system over the entire life of your solar project. Calculated by financial simulation.

name.example: Solar PV Energy Tax Credit - Personal

sum.description: The sum of all disbursements of the incentive over the entire life of your solar project in today's dollars. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

payback_period.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `cash`. The amount of time (in years) it takes to cover the upfront system price with monthly savings. Calculated by financial simulation.

loan_principal.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `loans`. Total loan taken in $. If there was no down payment, it will be equal to system price. Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 4 decimal places.

down_payment.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `loans`. Downpayment on the loan in $. Equals to `system_price - loan_principal`. Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 4 decimal places.

avg_monthly_savings.description: Only populated if `financing_option`is `loans`. The average monthly savings over the lifetime of the system, in $. Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

monthly_payment_first_month.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `loans`. First monthly payment on the loan in $ (Year 1, Month 1). Calculated by financial simulation. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

loans.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `loans`. List of all loans in this financing (calculated by financial simulation)

principal_percentage.description: Loan's principal percentage (in %). Rounded to 4 decimal places.

duration_months.description: Full loan duration, including all periods, in months

periods.description: List of all periods in this loan

interest_rate.description: interest rate for this period in %. Rounded to 4 decimal places.

epc_price_per_watt.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `lease`, `ppa`, or `levelized_ppa`. The price per watt paid to the EPC/installer. Rounded to 3 decimal places.

escalation.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `lease`, `ppa`, or `levelized_ppa`. The percent by which the `monthly_payment` (`lease`) or `solar_rate` (`ppa`) increases each year. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

monthly_payment.description:
Only populated if `financing_option` is `loans`, `lease`, `ppa`, or `levelized_ppa`. Rounded to 2 decimal places.
Loans - the first non-zero payment.
Lease - The monthly payment during the first year of a lease.
PPA - The estimated monthly payment during the first year of a PPA.
Levelized PPA - The estimated monthly payment during the first year of a levelized PPA.

solar_rate.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `ppa` or `levelized_ppa`. The price paid by the homeowner per kWh of production. Rounded to 3 decimal places.

specific_yield.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `lease`, `ppa`, or `levelized_ppa`. The specific yield (efficiency) of the design expressed in kWh/kWp. Calculated based on the performance simulation and used to help select values for `monthly_payment` (advanced lease) or `solar_rate` (advanced PPA). Rounded to 4 decimal places.

upfront_payment.description: Only populated if `financing_option` is `lease`, `ppa`, or `levelized_ppa`. The upfront payment prior to getting solar installed. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

prepaid_lease_factor.description: The lease factor for a prepaid lease. Only populated for financings associated with Participate Energy. Rounded to 7 decimal places.

financier.description: Information about the financier associated with this financing. Populated for both integrated and custom financier-backed financings.

type.description: Whether this financing uses an integrated or custom financier.

provider.description: Identifier for the financial institution. For custom financiers, this is the custom financier name.

status.description: Current state of the financing request. Only populated for integrated financiers.

approved_loan_amount.description: The maximum amount of money approved for a loan. Only populated for integrated financiers.

external.description: Values as they exist with the financial institution. Only populated for integrated financiers.

provider_status.description: The state of the financing request as retrieved from the provider before it is normalized to a fixed set of values for the `status`. These can differ between lenders.

request_id.description: Financier-issued ID, value depends on financier. Dividend - Project ID. EnFin - Application ID. GoodLeap TPO - Credit Application ID. Mosaic - Application ID. Sungage - Sungage ID. Unused by GoodLeap Loans, LightReach.

consumer_id.description: Financier-issued ID, value depends on financier. LightReach - Account ID. Unused by Dividend, EnFin, GoodLeap Loans, GoodLeap TPO, Mosaic, Sungage.

quote_id.description: Financier-issued ID, value depends on financier. LightReach - Quote ID. Mosaic - Offer ID. Unused by Dividend, EnFin, GoodLeap Loans, GoodLeap TPO, Sungage.

estimate_id.description: Financier-issued ID, value depends on financier. Mosaic - Estimate ID. Unused by Dividend, EnFin, GoodLeap Loans, GoodLeap TPO, LightReach, Sungage.

contract_signed_at.description: Timestamp when the contract was signed, as reported by the financier. Only populated for GoodLeap and LightReach when a contract signed event is received. Formatted as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC"

domestic_content_indicated.description: Whether domestic content was indicated for this financing. Only populated for integrated financiers.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the financing request was updated in UTC. Only populated for integrated financiers.

A plan set request contains information about a project necessary for Aurora to create a plan set document.

Creating a new plan set request requires the following:
- The id of a design that is ready to install. The design must include modules, and will be more accurate if the stringing and components are already present.
- The project that the design is associated with must have at least one image or document uploaded to the project as a project asset (see [Create Project Asset](ref:createprojectasset)).

All new plan set requests are created in `draft` status. See [Plan Sets](ref:plan-sets) for additional information on statuses.

year1_monthly_total_bill.description: Monthly total bill, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), from Jan - Dec. Total bill includes grid, fixed, demand charges as well as any applicable solar credits or net surplus compensation.

year1_monthly_grid_use_charges.description: Monthly grid charges, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), from Jan - Dec. These will include any applicable solar NEM credits.

year1_monthly_fixed_charges.description: Monthly fixed charges, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), from Jan - Dec. Fixed charges can be zero for utilities where solar credits can cover fixed charges.

year1_monthly_net_grid_consumption.description: Monthly amounts of energy consumed by the household from the grid from Jan - Dec, in kWh. These values account for PV and storage output.

year1_monthly_pv_consumption.description: Monthly amounts of PV-sourced energy consumed by the household from Jan - Dec, in kWh. Includes PV used directly and PV stored then discharged to the home. Does not include grid-sourced storage discharge.

year1_monthly_cash_net_surplus_compensat.description: Monthly net surplus compensation amounts, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), from Jan - Dec.

year1_feed_in_compensation.description: The total annual monetary compensation, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), for all energy exported to the grid in the first post-solar year. This differs from `year1_cash_net_surplus_compensation` in that it includes all exported energy compensation, rather than the net energy balance over the course of a billing period.

year1_monthly_total_pv_production.description: Monthly amounts of energy produced by the PV system from Jan - Dec, in kWh.

year1_monthly_fit_revenues.description: Monthly revenue, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), from the feed-in-tariff program, based on the total energy produced by the PV system, from Jan - Dec.

year1_cost_per_consumed_kwh.description: A value in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`) per kWh, result of dividing total annual bill (sum of `year1_monthly_total_bill`) by total annual consumption from the grid (sum of `year1_monthly_net_grid_consumption`).

utility_rate_name.description: The name of the utility rate.

year1_cash_net_surplus_compensation.description: The total annual monetary compensation, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`), for surplus energy in the first post-solar year.

year1_grid_use_kwh.description: The total annual energy consumed from the grid for the first post-solar year.

year1_grid_surplus_kwh.description: The total annual surplus energy generated for the first post-solar year.

loss_summary.description: Ordered list of energy loss steps from the performance simulation. Each entry represents one stage in the loss waterfall — the energy or irradiance remaining after applying that loss. Entries must be processed in order; loss_percentage is computed relative to the immediately preceding entry. An empty array is returned when no performance simulation has been run. See the [System Loss Settings API](ref:retrievedesignsystemlosssettings) for the mapping between editable loss settings and these loss-summary stages.

category.description: The loss group this entry belongs to.

name.description: Identifier for this loss step, as produced by the simulation engine.

value.description: Absolute irradiance or energy remaining at this step, rounded to the nearest integer.

units.description: Unit for the value field. kWh/m² for irradiance category entries (annual insolation); kWh for dc, ac, and other category entries.

loss_percentage.description: Percentage loss relative to the immediately preceding entry's value, rounded to 1 decimal place (e.g. -2.0 means 2% loss). Null only for the very first irradiance entry and the very first dc entry (reference points on different scales). All other entries — including the first ac and first other entries — have a non-null loss_percentage.

total_configured_loss_percentage.description: The cumulative loss from the user-configured derate inputs, displayed as "Estimated total loss" in Design Mode, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place (e.g. 8.6 means 8.6% total loss). Computed as a compound product of the configured per-loss derates (1 - Π(1 - lossᵢ)), not a simple sum. Excludes losses computed automatically by the simulation engine (e.g. the shading derate when the shading engine is enabled), so this value will differ from the full loss waterfall in loss_summary. Returns 0.0 when losses are configured but the computed net derate is zero (including when the shading engine excludes all applicable derates) — this is distinct from null, which means no performance simulation has been run or no system losses are configured.

y.description: Distance in the y direction in feet/meters from this array to the adjacent array, measured from the center of the top left module in each array. Positive numbers indicate modules higher on the roof.

preferred_solar_modules.description: List of solar module unique IDs. When set, this list overrides the tenant's starred/partner-scoped module list in AutoDesigner (Sales Mode and Design Mode) — the listed modules are always available regardless of starring or partner assignment. This is not an unconditional override, though, other restrictions still apply, so a module must be non-deprecated and available for the project's state to be selectable, and admin/unrestricted catalog searches bypass it entirely. Setting a deprecated module ID is rejected.

preferred_solar_inverters.description: List of solar inverter unique IDs. When set, this list overrides the tenant's starred/partner-scoped inverter list in AutoDesigner (Sales Mode and Design Mode), and overrides the tenant/partner's default Sales Mode inverter selection per inverter type (string vs. micro) — the listed inverters are always available regardless of starring or partner assignment. This is not an unconditional override, though, other restrictions still apply, so an inverter must be non-deprecated and available for the project's state to be selectable, and admin/unrestricted catalog searches bypass it entirely. Setting a deprecated inverter ID is rejected.

property_address.description: Full address of the project in the following format ('123 Main Street, Unit 12, City, CA, 93120'). Either address or a lat/long pair must be provided. If only address is provided, Aurora will set lat/long. If only lat/long are provided, Aurora will reverse GEO code the address. If neither are provided the request is rejected. If both are provided both are set.

latitude.description: Latitude of the site. If not both latitude and longitude are set (or both are null), the address will be used to geocode. Reject if only one is set.

longitude.description: Latitude of the site. If not both latitude and longitude are set (or both are null), the address will be used to geocode. Reject if only one is set.

project_type.description: Type of the project. Defaults to `"residential"`.

partner_id.description: Unique ID identifying the partner associated with the project. The owner of the project must be part of the partner. If the owner belongs to only one partner, the project will be associated with that partner on project creation if `partner_id` is not provided.

check_for_duplicates.description: If true, Aurora will check for duplicate projects based on the project address and/or latitude/longitude pair. If a duplicate is found, the request will be rejected with a 422 error. Defaults to `false`. This check follows the tenant settings for the scope of the check - it may be constrained to the partner or team level. If the check is disabled in the app, it will still be applied for API requests if the flag is set.

monthly_bill.description: An array of the monthly bills, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`). Null values allowed as "null".

monthly_energy.description: An array of the monthly energy in kWh. Null values allowed as "null".

interval_data.description: An array of the energy values for each 15/30/60 minute interval from the beginning to end of a common/leap year, in kWh. Null values allowed as "null". Array length must be exactly 8760, 8784, 17520, 17568, 35040, or 35136 values.

annual_energy.description: The total annual energy consumption in kWh. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1,000,000. Distributed across the year using a typical load profile for the project's location.

annual_bill.description: The total annual pre-solar electricity bill, denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`). Must be greater than 0, at least the lowest possible annual bill under the project's pre-solar utility rate (fixed charges plus any pool or EV usage), and at most the annual bill for 1,000,000 kWh. Converted to annual energy using the project's pre-solar utility rate, then distributed across the year using a typical load profile for the project's location.

utility_rate_escalation.description: The annual escalation of utility rates for the project, as a percentage (`4.0` means 4%). Can be sent on its own or together with one energy consumption value. Must be within the tenant's configured minimum and maximum for the project when the value changes. `null` is treated as not provided.

project_id.description: Unique ID identifying the project that the design request belongs to.

latitude.description: Latitude of the site. If not both latitude and longitude are set (or both are null), the address will be used to geocode. This determines the project marker and determines the building to be modeled. Rejected if only one (lat or long) is set.

longitude.description: Longitude of the site. If not both latitude and longitude are set (or both are null), the address will be used to geocode. This determines the project marker and determines the building to be modeled. Rejected if only one (lat or long) is set.

sla.description: ETA in minutes until request completion from submission time. Default is `180`. Set to `30` to expedite a request.

auto_accept.description: Whether or not it should be autoaccepted upon completion. Defaults to false.

roof_pitch.description: Angle of roof pitch in degrees, typically from 0 to 60. Defaults to null. This field is not used by our Expert Design Service in all tenants. For availability, please contact your Aurora account team.

number_of_stories.description: The height of the main structure of this request in stories. Defaults to null. This field is not used by our Expert Design Service in all tenants. For availability, please contact your Aurora account team.

external_provider_id.description: Unique ID of design provided by external provider.

project_id.description: Unique ID identifying the project that this design belongs to.

external_provider_id.description: Unique ID of duplicate design provided by external provider.

name.description: Name of the duplicate design. Defaults to name of original design with `" (Copy)"` appended.

milestone.description: The latest milestone to use for this design. Note that marking a design as sold will mark all other sold designs on the project as canceled. Setting this to "change_order" requires change_order_types to also be provided.

change_order_types.description: Required when milestone is "change_order". One or more reasons for the change order.

system_loss_settings.description: Map of loss name to percentage (0-100). Only the supplied losses are updated; any omitted loss is left unchanged. Unknown loss names are rejected.

shading.description: Shading loss as a percentage (0-100). Rejected when the shading engine is enabled.

mismatch.description: Module mismatch loss as a percentage (0-100).

wiring.description: DC wiring loss as a percentage (0-100).

light_induced_degradation.description: Light-induced degradation loss as a percentage (0-100).

rating.description: Nameplate rating loss as a percentage (0-100).

bill_of_materials.description: Array of racking bill of materials items for the design.  Providing an empty array will remove all racking items from the bill of materials.

sku.description: Manufacturer specific SKU of the component.

quantity.description: The number of components used in the design.

proposal_pdf_generation_job.description: Proposal pdf generation fields to run job from.

timezone.description: The timezone identifier used for dates and time rendered in the pdf. Defaults to UTC.

locale.description: The locale used for translated strings rendered in the pdf. Limited to the languages Aurora has translations for. Defaults to the tenant's locale.

pricing.description: Pricing fields to update. At least one field must be provided. `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, and `line_items` are mutually exclusive — provide one solar pricing field, not more than one. `line_items` sets per-component solar prices and sets the solar pricing mode to `price breakdown`. `storage_flat_system_price` and `storage_line_items` are mutually exclusive. Either storage field can be provided alone or alongside a solar pricing field. `heat_pump_flat_system_price` and `heat_pump_line_items` are mutually exclusive. Either heat pump field can be provided alone or alongside a solar or storage pricing field.

flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the design and sets the pricing mode to `flat system price`. Cannot be used with `price_per_watt` or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

price_per_watt.description: Sets the price per watt for the design and sets the pricing mode to `price per watt`. Cannot be used with `flat_system_price` or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`) per watt.

line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the design's solar price breakdown and sets the solar pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing solar line item in the design. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Cannot be used with `flat_system_price` or `price_per_watt`.

price.description: Price for one unit of the component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

storage_flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the storage design and sets the storage pricing mode to `flat system price`. Requires the design to have a storage design. Subject to the tenant's configured minimum/maximum storage flat price limits when set — a value outside those limits is rejected with a 422. Cannot be used with `storage_line_items`. Can be used alongside `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, or `line_items`. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

storage_line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the storage price breakdown and sets the storage pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing storage line item. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Requires the design to have a storage design. Cannot be used with `storage_flat_system_price`. Can be used alongside `flat_system_price`, `price_per_watt`, or `line_items`.

price.description: Price for one unit of the storage component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

heat_pump_flat_system_price.description: Sets the flat system price for the heat pump and sets the heat pump pricing mode to `flat system price`. Requires the design to have a heat pump. Subject to the tenant's configured minimum/maximum heat pump flat price limits when set — a value outside those limits is rejected with a 422. Cannot be used with `heat_pump_line_items`. Can be used alongside a solar or storage pricing field. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

heat_pump_line_items.description: Sets component unit prices in the heat pump price breakdown and sets the heat pump pricing mode to `price breakdown`. Send one item or several. `component_id` must match an existing heat pump line item. The submitted unit price replaces any existing quantity-based price tiers for that component. Requires the design to have a heat pump. Cannot be used with `heat_pump_flat_system_price`. Can be used alongside a solar or storage pricing field.

price.description: Price for one unit of the heat pump component. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

adder_value.description: The value of the adder. The unit depends on the type — flat adders are denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`); system_size adders are denominated in the tenant's configured currency per unit of `adder_system_size_basis` (per watt for `stc`, `ptc`, `ac`, and `storage_ac`; per watt-hour for `capacity_nominal`, `capacity_usable`, and `capacity_usable_ac`); percent adders are a percentage.

quantity.description: A multiplier for `adder_value`.

is_editable.description: Is `adder_value` editable on the Pricing page?

is_hidden.description: Is the adder hidden from homeowners?

is_quantity_editable.description: Is `quantity` editable on the Pricing page?

eligible_for_cbi.description: Is the adder eligible for price based incentives like the federal ITC? Assumed to be true if not specified.

prevent_manual_deletion.description: Prevent deletion of the adder on the Pricing page?

additional_charges.description: Array of additional charges to apply to the adder.

percentage.description: Percentage rate of the additional charge.

amount.description: The value of the incentive. Denominated in the tenant's configured currency (see `currency` on `GET /tenants/{id}`).

year_applied.description: Which year (relative to project life, starting with 0) the incentive will be applied in. Year 0 incentives will reduce the financed amount for a cash or loan financing.

apply_local_tax.description: Should local tax be applied to the incentive?

apply_national_tax.description: Should national tax be applied to the incentive?

proposal_template_id.description: Unique ID of proposal template id to generate proposal from.

design_id.description: The ID of the design that represents the system to be installed. The referenced design must have modules.
